interesting_fact_trainer.4_value: All new interesting facts may be found in the "Interesting Facts" window.@BLANK

interesting_facts.all_facts: Congratulations!\nYou've just opened the last interesting fact!
interesting_facts.1: The stripes of a tiger reach down into their skin.\n \n
interesting_facts.3: Snakes can sleep about 3 years running without any food.\n \n
interesting_facts.4: A blue chip stock is the stock of a well-established company having stable earnings and no extensive liabilities. The name "blue chip" came about because in the game of poker the blue chips have the highest value. Originally the term "blue chip" was used in reference to high-priced stocks, more commonly used today to refer to high-quality stocks.
interesting_facts.5: The Flag of the State of Alaska was designed by Benny Benson, a 13-year-old boy in 1927. The flag consists of eight gold stars, forming the Big Dipper and the North Star, on a dark blue field. By the way Alaska is larger than the next four largest states altogether. 17 of the 20 highest peaks in the United States are located in Alaska.
interesting_facts.6: Monaco's national orchestra is bigger than its army. By the way, although Monaco is known for its casinos but Monaco's own citizens are not allowed to gamble in the casinos.
interesting_facts.7: Hewlett and Packard tossed a coin to decide whether the company they founded would be called Hewlett-Packard or Packard-Hewlett. Packard won the coin toss but named their electronics manufacturing enterprise the "Hewlett-Packard Company" (now commonly referred to as "HP").
interesting_facts.8: Elvis Presley had a black belt of Karate. His first encounter with the art of Karate was in the Army when he was in Germany. Elvis once entered an Elvis "look alike" contest in a US burger bar and came only third!
interesting_facts.9: Honey is the only food that doesn't spoil.
interesting_facts.10: The first typewriter was built by William Burt in 1829 and was intended to be used for the blind.
interesting_facts.11: Our eyes are always the same size from birth, but our nose and ears never stop growing.
interesting_facts.12: The Coca-Cola name in China was first read as "Ke-kou-ke-la", meaning "Bite the wax tadpole" or "female horse stuffed with wax", depending on the dialect. Coke then researched 40,000 characters to find a phonetic equivalent "ko-kou-ko-le", translating into "happiness in the mouth."
interesting_facts.13: Why do onions make you cry? A fresh onion, when cut, releases a gas called propanethiol-Sin to the air. When this gas reaches your eyes, it mixes with the water in the eye to form a weak acid. This acid irritates the eye and causes the tear-producing glands to flood the eye with water in an attempt to wash away the irritant. These tears are what makes you look like you're crying.
interesting_facts.14: The microwave was invented after a researcher walked by a radar tube and a chocolate bar melted in his pocket.
interesting_facts.15: The credit card is rooted in the idea of allowing consumers to buy on time, which took hold in the 1920s. By the late 1940s, some department stores and gasoline companies had issued courtesy cards to their customers, granting them credit in advance of a purchase. Then, in 1950, businessman Francis Xavier McNamara was having lunch and discovered he had left his cash at home. He was so embarrassed that he invented the Diners Club, which issued a card good for meals, lodging and other travel expenses, the prototype for all future credit cards.
interesting_facts.17: The first cook book was written by the Greeks in 400 B.C.
interesting_facts.18: Fingernails grow nearly 4 times faster than toenails.
interesting_facts.19: You're born with 300 bones, but when you get to be an adult, you only have 206.
interesting_facts.20: Termites are affected by music. They will eat your house twice as fast if you play loud music.
interesting_facts.21: A "day" in Earth orbit is approximately 90 minutes, 45 minutes of daylight and 45 minutes of night, which means that astronauts in space can see 16 sunsets and 16 sunrises in 24 hours.
interesting_facts.22: If there were ever an ocean big enough, Saturn would be the only planet that could float, this is because its density is lighter than that of water (it is mostly gas).
interesting_facts.23: Iceland consumes more Coca-Cola per capita than any other nation.
interesting_facts.24: American Airlines saved $40,000 in 1987 by eliminating one olive from each salad served in first-class.
interesting_facts.25: Tomatoes were originally thought to be poisonous. But a Virginia doctor demonstrated that wasn't the case in 1733. Dr. Siccary ate the fruit and declared it was not only edible, but very delicious.
interesting_facts.26: Multiply 37,037 by any single number (1-9), then multiply that number by 3. Every digit in the answer will be the same as that first single number.
interesting_facts.27: Dogs have about 100 different facial expressions, most of them made with the ears.
interesting_facts.28: A duck's quack doesn't echo, and no one knows why.
interesting_facts.29: More women (80%) wash their hands in the bathroom than men (55%).
interesting_facts.30: In 10 minutes, a hurricane releases more energy than all the world's nuclear weapons combined.
interesting_facts.31: If a line was formed of all men of age 18 living in China and you had each man pass in front of you, how many days would it take to go through the whole line?  The answer is it would take forever. This line will never finish because new people will be added to the end of the line faster than they can pass in front of you.
interesting_facts.32: Red and white wine can be made using the same type of grape. The color of wine is not determined by the juice of the grape, which is almost always clear.  Rather, the color of wine is determined by the presence or absence of the grape skin during fermentation. Grapes with colored juice (for example Alicante Bouchet) are known as Teinturier. Red wine is made from red (or black) grapes, but it's red color is bestowed by a pro.
interesting_facts.33: The eyesight of a tiger in the dark is about six times better compared to humans.\n \n
interesting_facts.34: The sum of numbers on a roulette is equal to the "devil's" number 666.\n \n
interesting_facts.35: A whale's heart beats only 9 times per minute.\n \n
interesting_facts.36: Helium (a light gas and the second most abundant element in the universe) was first discovered in the Sun and only later found on Earth. Evidence of helium was detected in the spectrum of the Sun in 1868. Almost 27 years later a British chemist isolated helium on Earth.
interesting_facts.37: Brandy is one of the happier products of the long association between alcohol and accidents. In order to save storage space during shipping and to lessen the tax assessed by volume, medieval wine merchants removed water from wine. Their goal was to add the water removed by distillation back into the brandy just before consumption. Brandy was born when someone - perhaps a thirsty sailor - decided to drink the wine concentrate clean.
interesting_facts.38: More people die in a car on the way to the airport than in airplanes. So if you have reached the airport, take heart: the most dangerous part about flying is over.
interesting_facts.39: We almost do not feel the air around us, but that's not because it is very light. Weight of 1m3 of air is more than a kilo (1 ounce per cubic ft).
interesting_facts.40: Black and green tea is produced from the same tea leaves. The difference comes from the process of preparation. Leaves used for black tea are more heavily oxidized than green or oolong varieties.
interesting_facts.41: The Roman Empire was not the biggest empire in the world. By 1913, the British Empire covered about 36.6 million sq km (14.2 million square miles), or about a quarter of the Earth's total land area, which makes it the largest empire in history. Almost the same size was the Mongol Empire, which covered over 33 million sq km (12.6 million square miles) at its peak, which makes it the largest contiguous land empire in history. Both of these empires were more than 6 times larger than the Roman Empire.
interesting_facts.42: Although crocodiles look very dangerous and hippopotamuses look slow and bulky, hippos actually kill more people every year than crocodiles. Hippos can be extremely aggressive and even though they are bulky animals, they run faster on land than humans.
interesting_facts.43: Penicillin, perhaps the greatest accidental discovery of all time, was first discovered by Scottish bacteriologist Alexander Fleming in 1928 while researching the flu germ staphylococcus. Fleming was a brilliant but careless researcher and his lab was usually in chaos. After returning from a long vacation he noticed that a blue-green mould had killed all the bacteria in a Petri dish. It wasn't until 11 years later that Ernst Boris and Howard Walter Florey isolated the pure form of penicillin and began clinical trials.
interesting_facts.44: We swim much slower than we run and it seems like its more difficult to swim than to run because water resistance is greater than air resistance. But the fastest fish (the sailfish) is as fast as the fastest land animal (the cheetah). They both can run/swim with speeds of about 120 km/h (75 mile/h).
interesting_facts.45: Everyone knows that when the sun is just over the horizon, it is much bigger than at the peak. Many people think it is because of atmosphere effects. But, actually, this is not true. And the first statement is also not true -- the sun is not bigger when it is closer to the horizon. The sun's size does not change during the day - it is always the same size! Moreover you can completely cover that huge sun near the horizon with a one cent coin if you hold it at arm's length. The sun's large size is an illusion based on the fact that any object next to a line looks larger than when it does when in an empty space.
interesting_facts.46: All cyclones in the northern hemisphere rotate counterclockwise while all cyclones in the southern hemisphere rotate clockwise (as a result of the Corioles effect). But what happens when a cyclone crosses the equator? The answer is: cyclones never cross the equator. Cyclones do not normally form near the equator and then move in the direction of one of the poles.
interesting_facts.47: We often see Vikings represent with horned helmets. This general misconception that Viking warriors wore horned helmets was partly promulgated by the 19th century enthusiasts of the Gotiska Forbundet, founded in 1811 in Stockholm, with the aim of promoting the suitability of Norse mythology as high art and also for other ethnological and moral aims. Despite the depiction, however, there is no evidence that Viking Age Scandinavians ever wore horned helmets.
interesting_facts.48: The tallest mountain on Earth is not Mt. Everest. If you measure from the base to the peak of Mt. Mauna Kea in Hawaii, it is the tallest mountain on earth. It's more than 10km (>30,000ft) from its base (on the sea floor) to its tip. Only 4,245 m (13,796 ft) of that height is above sea level.
interesting_facts.49: If you are in a group of 40 people the chance that two in the group have the same birthday is not 40/365 (=11%) as one might think.  The probability is actually almost 90%. The chance will be even more than 97% if there are 50 people in the group.
interesting_facts.50: Milk from a camel can remain fresh for three months.\n \n
interesting_facts.51: A female armadillo can delay her childbirth for up to two years during times of stress.\n \n
interesting_facts.52: Do you know how many colors are in the rainbow? People in different countries give different answers. People from China will say that there are 5 colors in the rainbow. For people in the US it is more typical to say that there are 6 colors, while in Russia people say there are 7 colors. English speaking people also sometimes count the number of colors as 7 because Newton inserted indigo probably to increase the number of colors to seven - a theologically preferred number. Some sources now omit indigo, partly due to the poor ability of humans to distinguish colors in the blue portion of the visible spectrum.
interesting_facts.53: Human achievements are still very poor when considered on a cosmic scale. We still cannot even produce anything near to the high temperatures and pressures that exist in the stars. All the nuclear bombs and atom-smashers we have built are child's play in the great scheme of things. There is one area, however, where humans have achieved a result that has probably never been achieved before in the cosmos. In our labs we have produced lower temperatures than anywhere else in the universe. This is because there is vestigial radiation with a temperature of about 2-3 Kelvin degrees and there are no natural objects nor areas in the universe with much lower temperatures.
interesting_facts.54: The most common element on the Earth is Oxygen, and not because it is in the Earth's atmosphere. Rather, SiO2 is the most common mineral in Earth's crust, which makes Silica the second most common element on Earth.
interesting_facts.55: Many people think that SOS stands for "Save Our Souls", but this is incorrect. From the very beginning (1906), the SOS distress signal consisted of a continuous sequence of three dots, three dashes, three dots. "SOS" was just an easy way to remember the correct order of the dots and dashes.
interesting_facts.56: Before the US started construction on the Panama Canal, more than two and half million gallons of kerosene was spent for preparation of the work. But this kerosene was not used for any kind of machines - rather it was used to spray swamps as a part of an effort to eradicate the mosquitoes Aedes aegypti and anopheles, the carriers of yellow fever and malaria, respectively, from the canal zone. Death from yellow fever and malaria were the main reasons why the French workers who first attempted to build the Panama Canal failed.
interesting_facts.57: The cigarette lighter was invented before the friction match. The first lighter was invented in 1823 while the first friction match was not invented until 1827. An interesting note: the first matches were very dangerous - there was enough white phosphorus in one pack to kill a person.
interesting_facts.58: Because European fishermen never caught anything they recognized as eel young, the life cycle of the eel remained a mystery for a very long time. It wasn't until 1922 that a Danish professor discovered that all eels in Europe are actually born in the Sargasso Sea and make a long trip through the Gulf Stream across the ocean and, after three years, reach England. You may not have known that eel blood is extremely toxic. The toxin it contains is destroyed when cooked.  This is why you will never find sushi made with raw eel.
interesting_facts.59: The island of Manhattan was purchased in 1626 by Peter Minuit from the native Lenape Native Americans for $25 worth of trade goods -- $25 for all of the Big Apple, that now would cost billions. If Peter had instead put this $25 in a bank at 7% interest compounded continuously, he would have $3.6 trillion now -- which is more than the total current price of all the real estate in Manhattan.
interesting_facts.60: German and allied airforces launched bombing raids on each other's factories with ferocious regularity. The Germans devised a plan to deceive allied intelligence by building mock wooden factories painted in industrial colors, the hope being that the enemy would waste much of its precious ammunition on them. One day a lone British plane flew overhead, and dropped a lone wooden bomb.
interesting_facts.61: The thermal conductivity of glass is so small that you could hold two ends of a piece of glass that is fusing in the middle and the ends would not be even warm. An interesting fact is that the material with the highest thermal conductivity is not a metal like silver or copper (which have the highest thermal conductivity among all metals and 400 times that of glass). Rather, the material with the highest thermal conductivity is a material that looks so similar to glass - diamond. Diamond has the highest known thermal conductivity - about 6 times that of silver or copper. So if someone were to make a diamond tea-spoon it will be completely useless - you would get burned just after you put it in hot tea.
interesting_facts.62: There is a theory that the origins of the term "honeymoon" date back to the times of Ancient Babylon. In Babylonian culture, the father of the bride would provide his son in law with all the mead (a honey-based drink) he could drink during the first month of the marriage. And because their calendar was lunar based, this period was called moon. It was believed that drinking mead would increase the likelihood of producing a son.
